The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though appeal is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken-up for final disposal.

2. Challenging judgment and award dated 26.04.2018 passed by Senior Civil Judge and Addl.
MACT, Shahapur (for short 'tribunal') in MVC No.287/2014, this appeal is filed.
3. Shri Subhash Mallapur, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by insurer challenging award on quantum specifically assessment of loss of earning capacity.

Therefore, finding of tribunal regarding occurrence of accident, involving insured vehicle due to rash and negligent driving of its driver, claimant suffering NC: 2023:KHC-K:7387 injuries and liability of insurer to pay compensation are not in dispute.

4. It was submitted that as on date of accident i.e., 06.05.2014, claimant was a carpenter aged 22 years sustained fracture of left knee joint, assessed by PW.2 - Dr.Rajendra Kothari to have caused 55% physical disability in respect of left leg, tribunal considered loss of earning capacity at 41%,
which was excessive.
On said ground sought for allowing appeal and reducing compensation.
5. On other hand, Shri Sharanagouda V.Patil, learned counsel for respondent no.1/claimant sought to justify award.

It was submitted that compensation awarded was by taking lower monthly income of `6,000/- and compensation awarded towards pain and suffering and other heads was inadequate The Branch Manager vs Eshappa And Ors on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38523821/
2 and would off-set any scope for reduction.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for parties.
Perused impugned judgment and award.

From above and since only insurer is in appeal challenging quantum of compensation, insofar as functional disability, point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether compensation awarded towards future loss of income calls for reduction?"
8.

In order to establish loss of earning capacity, claimant relied on Wound Certificate, Disability Certificate, X-Ray Film, Discharge Summary, Medical Bills and Receipts etc. marked as Exs.P1 to P.10 respectively.
Claimant also examined Dr.Rajendra Kothari as PW.2.

While passing impugned award, tribunal considered age of claimant as 22 years on ground that there was no rebuttal evidence led by insurer and taking note of deposition of PW.2 that whole body disability was also 55%, tribunal proceeded to consider 41% as loss of earning capacity.
Though learned counsel for appellant/insurer seeks for reduction, same is not substantiated with specific ground.

Further,
assessment of functional disability or loss of NC: 2023:KHC-K:7387 earning capacity has to be by correlation of limb disability with occupation.
9. In instant case, claimant sustained fracture of left knee with restriction of knee movements.
There is no dispute that claimant was a Carpenter.
Normally carpenter would require to sit and squat while in occupation.
Besides above, PW.2 has specifically stated that whole body disability is also at 55%.
Considering said aspect, assessment of loss of earning capacity at 41% by tribunal cannot be stated to be either without reference to material on record or contrary to it.
Therefore, same would not call for any interference.
Point for consideration is answered in negative.

Consequently, following :
ORDER (i) Appeal is dismissed with costs.
Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to tribunal for payment.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7387 (ii) Balance shall be deposited within six weeks from date of receipt certified copy of this judgment.

Sd/-
